fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Tropical versus sidereal and pattern watching", "body": "Dan explained that he used the tropical zodiac with whole sign houses, and he defined sidereal as the zodiac tied to the actual constellations. He argued that tropical symbolism followed the seasons, so the meaning of Aries did not drift with the stars. One of the hosts agreed, saying the signs were conceptual metaphors for natural processes, and compared it to moving paintings between walls. Dan added that he sometimes borrowed sidereal ideas such as the fixed star Algol, and that any system could work if the practitioner watched for repeating patterns."}, {"title": "A day job, a podcast, and a band", "body": "Dan described juggling a day job, his Cosmic Keys podcast and his band Moonstone Quill, and he said a structured schedule had been surprisingly grounding after years of freelance instability. He told how he moved to Colorado in early 2020, played open mics with his bandmate Nate, and drove to Colorado Springs on impulse to buy a mandolin that Nate then picked up and played. Chance suggested a spirit team had nudged him there. The band played a run of shows in October 2020 before the second lockdown halted bookings."}, {"title": "How strong astrology really is", "body": "One of the hosts read a long run of astrology memes from the call-in line, and the group joked about sun signs, Scooby-Doo characters and zodiac behavior at restaurants. Dan said that if astrology were truly real it usually sat around a three out of ten, with only occasional tens, and that people claiming a constant ten were wrong. A host noted that Dan sometimes admitted on his own show that he did not believe in astrology that day. Dan argued the best astrologers offered possibilities rather than doom, and that natal charts were fixed while transiting planets moved across them."}, {"title": "Ghost stories, Hellier, and Randonautica", "body": "Gordy called in and told of a ghost tour on the Queen Mary, where his wife heard a voice and a stranger's phone was knocked from her hand, and where he described a smoky figure in a mirror that was dispelled by tall gold figures with staffs. The group then discussed the series Hellier and the Estes method of blindfolded spirit box listening. One speaker floated a theory that Randonautica and the Missing 411 cases might be connected, and another proposed that quartz deposits could hold a memory field for the earth."}, {"title": "Pluto, Uranus, and the coming decade", "body": "Asked about Pluto in Aquarius, Dan answered that it could be utopian or dystopian depending on perspective, tying it to the American Pluto return around 27 degrees Capricorn and to Venus and Mars gathering there in early March. He said Uranus in Taurus favored off the grid rebellion until 2025, then Gemini would push the fight toward the metaverse. Chance relayed a point from Michael Wann, made while talking with Mark Steeves, that a US Pluto return marks a new cycle, and he added his own view that bodies and land are one."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Dan Shukis is the astrologer host of Cosmic Keys Podcast, and a singer/songwriter/guitarist in the band Moonstone Quill.
